reviews.text: With so many past lives to choose from, the filmmakers of Infinite still repeated the same mistakes when there should have been limitless possibilities. Instead, it’s an endless exercise in suspense-free filmmaking.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Infinite is at times comedically convoluted, but thanks to brilliant world-building and stellar action setpieces, it’s riotously entertaining regardless.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Perhaps the movie’s biggest shortcoming is that it spends a lot of time talking about relationships from the past rather than building any meaningful new ones on screen.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: "Infinite" has all the elements you'd find in almost any action film. It just slightly misses the mark by not going all in and fully immersing the viewer in its reincarnation concept.
reviews.author: Ema Sasic

reviews.text: One of those grueling efforts that renders the science fiction genre about as much fun as a root canal sans anesthetics.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The writing is so haphazard and choppy, and it leapfrogs over what needs to be explained... you don't have any emotional investment.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Brainless. The only skills the reincarnated team of assassins retain are fighting skills, leaving any provocative questions about transmigration unaddressed and any interesting ideas unexplored.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: What follows is a ploddingly predictable slog through a confusing combination of sci-fi cliches and vaguely mystical mambo-jumbo that basically strings out a series of mindless pyrotechnic set-pieces.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: If you ever wondered what The Matrix would have been like if the lead was played by a fifty year old who was also kind of like Jason Bourne, here's your chance.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: If it's empty-vessel escapism you're after, this wonkily watchable affair will deliver what little you need.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: The visuals are spectacular, but things get increasingly derivative as they progress, and Jason Mantzoukas' ill-conceived comic-relief character falls clangingly flat.
reviews.author: Brad Newsome

reviews.text: If you understand any of it, please enlighten me, because I am in the dark.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The bad guys in Mark Wahlberg's reincarnation-themed action movie want to destroy the world so they never have to relive it all again. Having seen the film, I know the feeling
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: Given the bona fides of everyone involved, it seemed reasonable to expect an entertaining adventure -- and at worst, dumb fun -- but the final product underwhelms at even the low end of expectations.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: ...it unfurls more like an M. Night Shyamalan sci-fi misfire...
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: This action film about reincarnation tries to relive the plot beats of countless better films. The end result is a derivative, messy and forgettable film.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: Infinite boasts a high-concept story and extremely inventive action sequences, though Mark Wahlberg's performance leaves much to be desired.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: Playing around with the concept of reincarnation is certainly promising, but Infinite makes the plot absurd for no reason. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: I'll give points for finely crafted action sequences and a handful of bold casting choices, but beyond that, Infinite is decidedly, whole-heartedly average.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: It's exactly the kind of big, silly, occasionally exciting spectacle that have come to define summer movie season, for better or worse. There's even an opening for a sequel.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Woefully miscast, too derivative and not nearly exciting enough to overcome its fundamental blandness.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: This is a lot like the multiple-dimension thing of Jet Li's The One, in which...oh, never mind, it hardly matters, because to present Mark Wahlberg as the repository of Eastern thought makes me want to scream.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: "Infinite" is overcluttered with special effects and plagued by wooden acting and doesn't have one genuine character in it.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: I don't want to leave the impression "Infinite" is bad because in actuality, it's purely awful, a dopey actionioner filled with wonky science, inane dialogue and a plot so laughable it leaves you in hysterics.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Even though it fumbles a fascinating premise, I kind of liked Infinite. You've seen pieces of this movie before, it doesn't go particularly deep, but it kept me interested nevertheless.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: All the visual flourishes can't raise the narrative stakes of a movie rooted more in formula than character development or emotional payoff. By the end, you'll want to erase the memory of having watched it.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The pace of all the action gets tripped up by a convoluted plot that Infinite tangles instead of unfurls.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Frankly, it's a pity that there are infinite possibilities (no pun intended) that [Antoine] Fuqua can choose to explore in his latest film, given its reincarnation theme.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The premise of reincarnation and star power can't save this film from its sci -fi abyss
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Perhaps no director could breathe life into a film with such an absolutely dire script, and with such a sloppily superficial sense of its own worldbuilding and interior mythology.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Maybe "Infinite" isn't crazy, it's just misunderstood.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Occasionally explosive, but rarely coherent.
reviews.author: Johnny Loftus

reviews.text: Welcome to a movie that makes absolutely zero sense and didn't need to exist. From the acting to the story to the direction, there's nothing redeemable here.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Saying that schizophrenia is just midiagnosed past life recall is not great.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Stuck with an incomprehensible, half-baked idea and carried out with stale writing, mechanical acting, and relentless chase scenes and explosions, this sci-fi action movie is an almost total failure.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Knee-jerk clichés abound in a shameless retread of The Matrix in which many levels of storytelling ineptitude are the only depth on offer. Can Hollywood please stop reincarnating the same old movies?
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Things get more ludicrous as they unfold, but never to the point of being goofy fun.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Fuqua does what he can to sprinkle garnishing on cold leftovers, but the script barely holds together, and seems to emanate from an alternate reality where no other sci-fi films or games were released in the last 25 years.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: High octane action can't save this messy would-be franchise starter
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: We desperately need more original, high concept action films, and kudos to Fuqua for attempting, but the script needed to go through a few different lifetimes before being ready for production.
reviews.author: Sean Price

reviews.text: A particularly pathetic example of big-budget sci-fi folderol, a woebegone attempt at a CGI-heavy action thriller that leaves egg on everyone's face.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A lazy, could've-been-inventive affair that lacks any charm to compensate for the by-the-numbers material.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Viewed at home, from the perspective of the couch, the effects are smaller, the holes in the story bigger, the acting infinitely more ridiculous.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: A hodgepodge of ideas better executed elsewhere and dragged down by an uninterested lead actor.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: It keeps stalling out even when it switches transportation modes.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Mostly... Infinite feels like a depressing fable about the movie industry.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Feels like Hollywood took another crack at bringing Assassins' Creed to life but somehow worse
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: While the film had an interesting premise, a strong cast and a seasoned director, the plot was difficult to follow which confused me quite a bit.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Infinite has an intriguing set-up that's fumbled by a poorly written script. Dylan O'Brien and Mark Wahlberg needed to reverse roles as the protagonist.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It's the worst kind of soulless committee-made product, lazy and risk-free, that need never and will never be thought of again. Infinite? Not even close.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: There just isn't enough here to recommend 'Infinite' as more than background noise for a lazy afternoon.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: Infinite is an easy watch, but the predictable plot and forgettable script come together to create an unmemorable experience.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Paramount+ has finally released its first major in-house exclusive movie, but it's an understatement to say that Infinite could be better.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Infinite flattens a high-stakes battle of good and evil into airless action of little consequence peopled by characters that amount to even less.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: "Infinite" is entertaining, transforming into a YA adventure for adult audiences, with the endeavor working especially hard to build enough momentum for future installments.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Rather than crafting a high-concept science-fiction marvel, Fuqua's "Infinite" relies on shoddy VFX and ropey world-building for the worst film of his career.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Another "was supposed to be in multiplexes" streaming premiere that's so bad it qualifies as a mitzvah to movie theaters.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Remembering one's past lives could only be made much worse by having watched this movie in one of them.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Logic isn't the point, and unfortunately, the potential of this premise isn't, either.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: All things considered, Infinite is the perfect content for Paramount+: big budget theatrics and low stakes drama.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Mark Wahlberg plays a reincarnated Japanese blacksmith who uses his sword to stab a plane. What else do you need to say?
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: I like Wahlberg just fine, but he is sorely miscast as the lead character.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: [I]t coalesces as a convoluted and tired "chosen one" story that inspires an empty performance from Mark Wahlberg and some world-class scenery chewing from Chiwetel Ejiofor.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: The more you start to nitpick this movie, the more egregious its plot holes appear, until the whole thing collapses in on itself.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: There's nothing entertaining about Infinite. It just sits there, lifeless, hoping to become a full-blown franchise with sequels galore.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Paramount decided to move it to Paramount+ where this generic, derivative nonsense will probably fit better anyway. It already plays more like something the Netflix algorithm burped up on an off-cycle.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Between the stars and the action, ﻿Infinite﻿ has plenty of elements working in its favor, but the overall execution still leaves one wanting.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: It's tacky product, fully deserving its fate of being dumped to also-ran streaming status.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: When all is said and done, Infinite is a prime summer blockbuster whose mindlessness and similarities to other science fiction thrillers don't prevent it from being dull or from galvanizing audiences for a follow-up.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Wahlberg, who usually has a way with a cynical wisecrack, seems to sprain muscles trying to sell his character's attempts at light-witted banter.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Runs out of lives.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Infinite never escapes the tiredness of its by-the-numbers mechanics.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: "Infinite" has some impressive set pieces combining practical effects and CGI, and the terrific cast approaches the material with grim-faced sincerity, but it's ultimately a big bag of nonsense wrapped in glossy packaging.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: What Infinite fatally lacks is personality. It's all sci-fi table setting all the time, racing through introductions and plot points at a mercenary pace, its wheel manned by a star whose default mode for this kind of movie is hunky frowning.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: "Infinite" only runs 106 minutes, but you'd do anything not to live through it again.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: This feels like a paycheck job all around, and Bathurst speaks for everyone when he proclaims that "Newer is almost never better."
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: The film plays like an overcomplicated imitator of The Matrix that never pauses long enough to foster interest in a single character. It's busy and bombastic but dull, explosive and assaultive but never exciting...
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: The problem with Antoine Fuqua's spin on the formula is that it's mostly formula and hardly any spin.
reviews.author: Devika Girish

reviews.text: I liked it just enough to like it but not enough to think anybody else will.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: If Mark Wahlberg's existential narration feels like it's on the verge of selling you something, it is. He's trying to close the deal on how smoothly "Infinite" can go down if you surrender to its deeply, incessantly goofy pleasures. And he succeeds.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: In the comfort of your home,Infiniteis an exciting diversion but hardly the kind of film you'll want to live through again and again.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: "Infinite" hops from set-piece to set-piece, with director Antoine Fuqua - a long way from "Training Day" - pushing the action sequences well past the point of credibility and occasionally into hilarity.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

synopsis: For Evan McCauley (Mark Wahlberg), skills he has never learned and memories of places he has never visited haunt his daily life. Self-medicated and on the brink of a mental breakdown, Evan is sought by a secret group that call themselves “Infinites,” revealing to him that his memories may be real--but they are from multiple past lives. The Infinites bring Evan into their extraordinary world, where a gifted few are given the ability to be reborn with their memories and knowledge accumulated over centuries. With critical secrets buried in his past, Evan must work with the Infinites to unlock the answers in his memories in a race against time to save humanity from one of their own (Chiwetel Ejiofor) who seeks to end all life to stop what he views as the cursed, endless cycle of reincarnation.
